explanation.text: The Logic: Exchange-traded futures contracts are marked to market daily under standard exchange practice. At each day's close, open positions are revalued at the day's settlement price and the resulting gains or losses are debited from or credited to participant margin accounts the same day. This continuous daily settlement mechanism is what prevents the build-up of unsettled counterparty exposure over the life of the contract. The Trap: 'Settles only at expiry' describes forwards, not exchange-traded futures. Weekly MTM and 'never happens' both contradict standard futures market mechanics. Note: The cited NISM Series XXI-A PMS Distributors workbook treats MTM margin only as the notional loss an outstanding trade has suffered during a specified period; it does not explicitly state that futures are marked to market and settled daily. The framing above is presented as general derivatives/exchange-practice knowledge rather than as a workbook citation.
